title: Rename the binary name the two Python packages actually spawn — the only brand occurrence Python executes — and change nothing else they mention
one_line: In `python/omp-rpc` and `python/robomp` exactly two source lines mint the binary name (`client.py:455` and `config.py:95`), plus two shipped-config overrides the plan's grep cannot see (`docker-compose.yml:81` and `.env.example:185`) that would silently defeat both edits; every other `omp` in `python/**` is a Unix group that is materialized on real hosts, a container-sandbox on-disk layout, or the CLI's own config dir owned by W4/W6, and all of them stay. The Python packages ship in the same release as W9 because between a TS-only rename and a Python rename there is a window in which the new binary has no `omp` command and the Python clients still call one.
user_visible_effect: The typed RPC client and the robomp triage bot spawn the renamed binary by default instead of failing with FileNotFoundError on `omp`. Users who set `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND` keep working untouched — it remains the override. Users who upgraded the CLI but not these two Python packages see every RPC call fail with 'omp: command not found'; shipping both renames in one release is what removes that window.

files_touched.change: Line 455, the ONLY line in this file that mints a binary name: `executable: str = "omp",` in `RpcClient.__init__` becomes `executable: str = "<new>",`. This is one of two source sites in all of `python/**`; verified `git grep -c '"omp"' -- python/omp-rpc/src/omp_rpc/client.py` == 1, so this edit takes the file to zero.
files_touched.note: The binary name comes from W9. Do not hardcode it here independently — read the value W9 sets in `packages/coding-agent/package.json:28` / `scripts/ci-release-publish.ts:165` and use the same token, or the two drift and the RPC client spawns a command no release installs. There is no shared constant across the language boundary, so the agreement gate below is the only thing holding them together.

files_touched.change: Line 95, the second and last source site: `omp_command: str = Field("omp", alias="ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND")` becomes `Field("<new>", alias="ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND")`. The pydantic FIELD name `omp_command` and the ALIAS `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND` both STAY — N16 keeps the `OMP_*` environment family permanently, and `worker.py:647` reads `settings.omp_command` by field name. Only the string default changes.
files_touched.note: Changing the alias or the field name is the N16 violation: it would orphan every `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND` already set in a user's `.env`, systemd unit or compose file, with no error and no fallback. Verified `git grep -n 'omp_command' -- python/robomp/src` returns exactly 2 hits — the definition here and the single consumer at `worker.py:647`.

files_touched.change: Lines 1044 and 1061 must NOT be mechanically renamed. Line 1044 passes `executable="omp"` explicitly into `RpcClient(...)` and line 1061 asserts the resulting `client.command` tuple starts with `"omp"` — that is an explicit value echoed back, which AGENTS.md bans as a success-passthrough. Delete both: drop the `executable=` argument so the test exercises the real default, and assert `client.command[0] == "<new>"` with the literal new name. That converts a worthless echo into the transformation assertion the item's test contract actually asks for.
files_touched.note: If instead you only swap the string in both places, the test stays green under BOTH names and proves nothing — the exact failure mode W11 warns about. Keeping the literal in this one test is deliberate: it is the pin that a default-value change cannot silently invalidate.

files_touched.change: Line 81, `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND: omp`, under the `# --- container-fixed paths ---` header (line 80), becomes `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND: <new>`. THIS IS THE FINDING THE PLAN MISSES. A value set in a compose service environment overrides the pydantic default, so editing `config.py:95` alone changes nothing in the shipped container: robomp keeps spawning the old binary while every grep-based check reports the item done.
files_touched.note: Owned by neither this plan nor W10 — W10's location list is `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dockerignore`, `Dockerfile.robomp`, `scripts/ci-update-brew-formula.ts`, `flake.nix` and `scripts/install-tests/*`, and this file is not among them. Same structural shape as §3.1: a consumer reads a name from a constant while a producer hardcodes the literal somewhere else, and the two are checked by nothing.

files_touched.change: Line 185, `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND=omp`, becomes `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND=<new>`, and the two comment lines above it (183-184, which describe 'the omp binary' and the shim) are updated to the new name. This file is the documented default users copy; leaving it naming a command the image no longer installs ships a broken example.
files_touched.note: Not in the plan's inventory either. It is documentation-by-example, so it must agree with `config.py:95` or it becomes the third disagreeing site.

files_touched.change: Change THREE lines: `:8` description 'Typed Python client for the omp coding-agent RPC protocol'; `:14` keywords, the `"omp"` element; `:26` `Homepage = "https://omp.sh/"`. DO NOT change `:6` `name = "omp-rpc"` — the open-questions table at the end of M5 decides that one and its stated default is KEEP `omp-rpc` permanently, because renaming it breaks every existing `pip install omp-rpc`.
files_touched.note: `:26` is coupled to N9 and must not be renamed on its own schedule: it is the same `https://omp.sh/` value as `APP_URL` at `packages/utils/src/dirs.ts:24`, and the risk table rules that URL frozen until a new domain actually resolves. Rename it in the same commit as N9's decision, or leave it. Separately, `:27` and `:28` carry `https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi` — invisible to `git grep -n 'omp'` because the string `oh-my-pi` does not contain the substring `omp`.

files_touched.change: Change ONE line: `:8` description 'Self-hosted GitHub triage/fix bot driving omp --mode rpc'. DO NOT change `:6` `name = "robomp"` and DO NOT change `:22` `"omp-rpc>=0.1.0"`.
files_touched.note: `:22` is the single sharpest trap in this item and the plan lists it as a rename site. It is a PEP 508 requirement on the omp-rpc DISTRIBUTION name. If `omp-rpc` is kept — the open-question default — then renaming this to `ultraworkers-rpc` makes robomp's dependency unresolvable and `uv pip install python/robomp` fails hard at resolve time, taking the whole bot down. The line is COUPLED to the distribution-name decision, not a rename site. The same reasoning applies to `Dockerfile:164` (`pip install /tmp/wheels/omp_rpc-*.whl`), which resolves against the built wheel filename.

files_touched.change: NOTHING IS EDITED IN THIS FILE. It contains two `"omp"` occurrences and both stay verbatim: `:211` `gid = grp.getgrnam("omp").gr_gid` and `:664` `extra_groups=["omp"]`. Separately, `:145`, `:168`, `:209` reference `_AGENT_HOME / ".omp"` and `_AGENT_HOME / ".omp/agent"` — also untouched, see the note.
files_touched.note: The two `"omp"` hits are the N13 machine-level Unix group (GID 2000, created by `entrypoint.sh:25`), already materialized on every running host. The three `.omp` path hits are a DIFFERENT identity that the plan has no category for: `_AGENT_HOME = Path("/srv/agent-home")` at `:136` is the CLI's own config dir, i.e. `CONFIG_DIR_NAME` from `dirs.ts:27`, owned by W4's dual-root reader and W6's flip. Leaving them on `~/.omp` is CORRECT during the transition precisely because W4 keeps reading the legacy root. A broad `.omp` rename in `python/**` would move robomp's staging off the root the CLI is still reading — a silent, container-only break.

files_touched.change: NOTHING IS EDITED IN THIS FILE. `:549` and `:588` `(base / "omp").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` stay. So do `:500` and `:574` (`.omp-tmp`), `:541` and `:584` (`.omp-xdg`), `:759` (`.omp-xdg/cache`), and `:899`/`:1047` (`.omp-session`, `.omp-session-{tag}`).

Verified across all of `python/`: the `.omp*` literal family is 63 quoted occurrences in 12 files (`.omp-xdg` 30, `.omp-tmp` 14, `.omp-session` 10, `.omp` 6, `.omp-session-v1.2.3` 2, `.omp-session-v1.2.4` 1), against the 12 the plan counts. Extend the keep-list entries to name the whole family or a future pass will rediscover them one at a time.

files_touched.note: Not in the plan's inventory at all, but it is the same on-disk identity and would be caught by any sweep of the `.omp*` family. Listed here so the keep-list is complete rather than so it can be edited.

files_touched.change: NOTHING IS EDITED. Both identity families in this file stay: the N13 Unix group (`:25` `groupadd -f -g 2000 omp`, `:28` `user="omp-$i"`, `:29`, `:32`, `:33`, `:53` `chown -R root:omp`) AND the W4/W6 CLI config dir (`:60`, `:61`, `:65`, `:66`, `:77`, `:78`, `:79`, `:80`, `:81`, all under `/srv/agent-home/.omp`).
files_touched.note: This file is the clearest argument for enumerating keep sites by identity rather than by pattern: one file holds two families with opposite dispositions, and `groupadd -f` at `:25` swallows the rename silently — `groupadd -f -g 2000 <new>` does not error when the group already exists, so the container still exits 0 while `chown -R root:<new>` at `:53` has quietly orphaned `/data` from every slot user.

files_touched.change: NOTHING IS EDITED. All five occurrences (`:26`, `:34`, `:36`, `:40`, `:45`) stay, and this file is the ONLY automated net standing between the N13 Unix-group decision and a future well-meaning `sed`.
files_touched.note: The plan groups all five as 'group identity, do not touch', which is the safe call but over-broad: `:36` and `:40` (`group="omp"`, asserting `call.kwargs["group"] == "omp"`) genuinely defend the group name, whereas `:26`, `:34` and `:45` pass `executable="omp"` as an INERT placeholder in a test about user/group kwargs — renaming those three would be harmless. The reason to still leave all five alone is that the test file is a unit of intent: partially rewriting it invites the next reader to 'finish' it. AGENTS.md is explicit that these assertions are the only guard against renaming the group.

LINE NUMBERS CORRECTED — the plan says 759, 828, 1071, 1073, 1075, 1105, 1107, 1109. All eight are off by exactly +1 on HEAD 84cbac9, verified with `grep -n '"omp"' python/robomp/tests/test_sandbox.py`. An engineer trusting the plan edits one line above each target.

steps.instruction: Take the binary name from W9, not from this plan. W9 (`packages/coding-agent/package.json:28`, `scripts/ci-release-publish.ts:165`) is what decides the installed command; the token used here must be that exact string. Change `executable: str = "omp",` to `executable: str = "<new>",`. This is one of only two source lines in all of `python/**` that mint a binary name, so run `git grep -c '"omp"' -- python/omp-rpc/src/omp_rpc/client.py` and confirm it prints nothing (the file is now clean) rather than assuming the edit landed.

Change ONLY the string default in `omp_command: str = Field("omp", alias="ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND")` → `Field("<new>", alias="ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND")`. The pydantic field name and the `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND` alias are N16-protected and stay exactly as they are. Verify the consumer still resolves with `git grep -n 'omp_command' -- python/robomp/src` returning exactly 2 hits: the definition and `worker.py:647`.

The step the plan omits, and the one that decides whether this item did anything at all. Under the `# --- container-fixed paths ---` header, change `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND: omp` to `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND: <new>`. An env var in a compose service environment OVERRIDES the pydantic default from step 2, so if you stop at step 2 the shipped container keeps spawning the old binary — with every grep-based acceptance check in the plan reporting the work as done. Do this before touching any metadata, and confirm with the three-way agreement gate below.

Change `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND=omp` to `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND=<new>`, and update the two comment lines above it (183-184) that describe 'the omp binary' and the shipped shim. This is the fourth site that must agree; it is a documented default, so it is also user-visible. After this step, run the three-way agreement gate — it now covers four sources and must print all four as identical.

Rewrite, do not rename. Delete the explicit `executable="omp",` argument at :1044 and the corresponding `"omp",` expectation at :1061 so the test exercises the real default, then assert `client.command[0] == "<new>"` with the literal new name. Mechanically swapping both strings leaves a test that passes under either name and defends nothing — AGENTS.md bans exactly that echo. This is the transformation assertion the item's test contract calls for, and it is the only automated proof anywhere that the DEFAULT moved.

Metadata, and only the descriptive half of it. In `python/omp-rpc/pyproject.toml` change `:8` (description), `:14` (the `"omp"` keyword element) and `:26` (`Homepage`). Leave `:6` `name = "omp-rpc"` alone — that is the published distribution name, decided by the open-questions table whose default is to keep it permanently. For `:26` specifically, apply the N9 gate: it is the same `https://omp.sh/` value as `APP_URL` at `dirs.ts:24` and must not move until a new domain resolves; if N9 has not been decided, leave `:26` as it is and say so in the commit message rather than renaming it on a guess.

Step 6 is where a reader is most likely to 'finish the job' on :22; it is a PEP 508 requirement on the omp-rpc distribution name, and because :6 keeps that name, renaming the requirement makes robomp unresolvable at install time. Extend the `do_not_rename` keep-list (owned by W7, file `scripts/rename/keep-list.txt`) with the four Python identities this item verified, because the plan's N13/N15 entries under-describe them. Confirm all 8 keep sites in `sandbox.py`, `worker.py`, `test_sandbox.py`, `test_user_group.py` and `test_worker.py` are byte-identical to HEAD.

Do not touch this file, and do not let a formatter or a broad replace reach it. `test_user_group.py:26,34,36,40,45` and `test_worker.py:465` are the only automated nets for the N13 Unix-group decision; `test_sandbox.py`'s 8 are the only nets for the sandbox layout. Verify with `git diff --stat` that these four test files are absent from the change before committing.

code_shape: Four string literals change, all of them values rather than structure. (1) `python/omp-rpc/src/omp_rpc/client.py:455` — a Python default parameter in a keyword-only `__init__` signature: `executable: str = "omp"` → `executable: str = "ultraworkers"`. No type change, no signature reordering, no import. (2) `python/robomp/src/config.py:95` — a pydantic v2 `Field` default: `omp_command: str = Field("omp", alias="ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND")` → `Field("ultraworkers", alias="ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND")`. The field name and alias are N16-frozen; only the first positional argument moves. (3) `python/robomp/docker-compose.yml:81` and `.env.example:185` — YAML and dotenv values of the same environment variable, which override (2) at runtime. (4) Four descriptive strings in two `pyproject.toml` files. Everything else in `python/**` is untouched, which is the point: `git diff` on this item should be about 10 added and 10 removed lines across 7 files, and every other file in `python/` should not appear. There is no new module, no new constant, no new import, and no cross-language sharing mechanism — the TS and Python sides hold the same string twice and are held together only by the agreement gate.
test_contract:
Three contracts, one per failure the item exists to prevent.

(1) THE SPAWNED DEFAULT MOVED. Construct `RpcClient()` with no `executable` argument and assert the command it would run starts with the new binary name. This is a transformation assertion over a value the code computes, not an existence check and not an echo of a value the test supplied. It is the ONLY automated proof in the repository that the default changed, because before step 5 the existing test passes its own value in and gets it back. Failing consumer: the RPC client spawns a command that no release installs, and every call dies with FileNotFoundError at the first request.

(2) THE OVERRIDE STILL WINS. Set `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND` to an explicit value, load `Settings`, and assert `settings.omp_command` returns the override rather than the default. This is the documented escape hatch and the only thing standing between a user on an old image and a total outage. It must be a second, distinct case in the same test — a first case alone cannot distinguish 'the default changed' from 'the field stopped reading the environment at all', which is the same outward symptom.

(3) THE KEEP SETS ARE UNTOUCHED. Gate 1's per-file counts (5,2,2,8,3) plus the zero-count on the three changed files. This is a negative contract: the failure it prevents is a rename that looks like progress and is a `KeyError` at container start, or a `Permission denied` on `/data` for every slot user. Existing coverage in `test_user_group.py` and `test_worker.py:465` is retained, not replaced.

Not tested, and deliberately: nothing in this repository executes `docker-compose.yml`, so gate 3 is a static string-agreement check and cannot observe a real container spawn. If a container-level proof is wanted, it needs a compose smoke run, which is out of scope here — say so rather than implying the gate is behavioural.

gate:
Three gates, all executed from the repo root, all verified to produce the stated result on HEAD 84cbac9 BEFORE any edit. Gates 1 and 2 are tripwires (red now, green after the work); gate 3 is an invariant (green now, green after, RED on a partial rename) and is the one that catches the failure this item is actually about.

--- GATE 1 — THE SPLIT (tripwire: RED today) ---
CHANGED=$(git grep -c '"omp"' -- python/omp-rpc/src/omp_rpc/client.py python/robomp/src/config.py python/omp-rpc/tests/test_client.py 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
KEPT=$(git grep -c '"omp"' -- python/omp-rpc/tests/test_user_group.py python/robomp/src/worker.py python/robomp/src/sandbox.py python/robomp/tests/test_sandbox.py python/robomp/tests/test_worker.py 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' | cut -d: -f2 | paste -sd, -)
echo "set_i_files_still_matching=$CHANGED keep_counts=$KEPT"
[ "$CHANGED" = "0" ] && [ "$KEPT" = "5,2,2,8,3" ]

Verified output today: `set_i_files_still_matching=3 keep_counts=5,2,2,8,3` → RED, as designed. The residual total is 20, not 24, and the keep counts are pinned PER FILE so that renaming a Unix group or a sandbox path cannot be masked by deleting a different keep site. `git grep -c` prints nothing for a zero-count file, which is why the changed-file check counts LINES OF OUTPUT (3 today) rather than summing hits.

--- GATE 2 — NO SHIPPED FILE PINS THE OLD NAME (tripwire: RED today) ---
OV=$(git grep -ohE 'ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND[=:][[:space:]]*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*' -- python/robomp/docker-compose.yml python/robomp/.env.example | awk -F'[=:] *' '{print $2}' | paste -sd, -)
echo "shipped_overrides=[$OV]"; [ "$OV" = "ultraworkers,ultraworkers" ]

Verified output today: `shipped_overrides=[omp,omp]` → RED, as designed. This is the gate that does not exist in the plan. It targets the two files the `"omp"` grep cannot see, because there the value is unquoted-at-line-start and preceded by the variable name.

--- GATE 3 — FOUR-WAY NAME AGREEMENT (invariant: GREEN today, RED on a partial rename) ---
C=$(grep -oE 'executable: str = "[^"]+"' python/omp-rpc/src/omp_rpc/client.py | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | tr -d '"')
R=$(grep -oE 'omp_command: str = Field\("[^"]+"' python/robomp/src/config.py | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | tr -d '"')
D=$(grep -oE 'ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND: *[^ ]+' python/robomp/docker-compose.yml | awk '{print $2}')
E=$(grep -oE 'ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND=[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*' python/robomp/.env.example | cut -d= -f2)
echo "client=$C config=$R compose=$D env=$E"
{ [ -n "$C" ] && [ "$C" = "$R" ] && [ "$C" = "$D" ] && [ "$C" = "$E" ]; }

Verified output today: `client=omp config=omp compose=omp env=omp` → GREEN (all four agree today). This gate is the structural mirror of §3.1: a consumer reads a name from a constant while a producer hardcodes the literal elsewhere, and nothing executes either. It stays green through a correct rename and goes red the moment one of the four is missed — most valuably if `config.py` is changed and `docker-compose.yml` is not, which is precisely the mistake gate 1 alone would report as success.

--- ENVIRONMENT-SUFFIXED GATE — the behavioural one, WITH a runnable-prefix check ---

gate_can_fail:
Yes, and the reason each of the three can fail is different.

GATE 1 fails the moment a set-(i) site is missed, and — because the keep counts are per file rather than a single total — it also fails if the engineer satisfies '20 remain' by renaming a Unix group or a sandbox path. That second failure mode is the one the plan's total-count check would miss entirely: dropping `test_user_group.py` from 5 to 0 and `test_sandbox.py` from 8 to 3 both land on exactly 20. Verified red today (`set_i_files_still_matching=3`).

GATE 2 fails if `docker-compose.yml` or `.env.example` still names the old command. This is the gate for a mistake the plan does not contain, and the mistake it catches is silent: the container starts, robomp boots, and the first RPC spawn is the only evidence. Verified red today (`shipped_overrides=[omp,omp]`).

GATE 3 fails on a PARTIAL rename — any one of the four sources changed without the other three. It is the only gate here that stays green before and after and therefore functions as a regression net rather than a progress indicator. Verified green today (`client=omp config=omp compose=omp env=omp`); it must be green again only when all four read the new name.

Stated plainly so they are not over-trusted: the environment-gated pytest run cannot fail on a rename at all if the prefix is skipped — which is why the prefix exits 2 with NOT-RUNNABLE rather than falling through. `bun run check:ts` is in the plan's command line and is STRUCTURALLY BLIND here: it filters `./packages/*` and oxlint is JS/TS only, so no edit to any file in this item can turn it red. It must not be reported as evidence for this work. Nothing in this repository executes `docker-compose.yml`, so gate 3 is a static string comparison and not a behavioural proof that a container spawns the right command — a real container smoke run is the only thing that would be, and it is out of scope.
depends_on: W9 (the binary name W9 installs is the value these four sites must carry — W13p cannot name the new command without W9, and shipping W9 without W13p leaves the Python clients calling a command that no longer exists)
blocks: W10 (its Docker work builds the image whose `/usr/local/bin/omp` shim at Dockerfile:180 and ENTRYPOINT at :216 is what `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND` names; if W10 renames the shim and this item has not updated docker-compose.yml:81, the robomp image is built pointing at a command it no longer contains)
effort: S, not the plan's M — and the plan overcounts for a defensible reason while undercounting the inventory. The edits themselves are 6 string values across 4 code files plus 4 descriptive strings across 2 manifests: about 10 added and 10 removed lines in 7 files, with roughly 150 real `omp` occurrences left deliberately untouched. What the plan priced as M is the deliberation of enumerating 24 occurrences into three sets, and that enumeration is already done and verified here (4 / 8 / 12, per-file counts pinned), so the expensive half of the plan's estimate is spent. What it missed — the compose override, the `.omp*` family being 108 rather than 12, the `~/.omp` config-dir category, and the `robomp:22` dependency coupling — is discovery cost that this spec has already paid. Realistically half a day: 2-3 hours of edits, 1 hour reconciling the keep-list with W7's `scripts/rename/keep-list.txt`, 1 hour of gates, and the rest waiting on the two open questions below. The one thing that can stretch it is container verification, which cannot be done from this repository at all.
risk:
Highest consequence, and the one the plan names correctly: editing only `client.py:455` and `config.py:95` and calling it done. The `"omp"` grep drops to exactly 20, every acceptance criterion in §3.3 passes, and the shipped robomp container still spawns `omp` — because `docker-compose.yml:81` overrides the pydantic default and the plan's grep cannot see an unquoted value that follows a variable name. Same structural shape as §3.1, which is why it is easy to miss here too: a consumer reads a name from a constant, a producer hardcodes the literal somewhere else, and nothing in the repository executes either.

Second, and sharper than a missing edit: renaming `python/robomp/pyproject.toml:22` from `"omp-rpc>=0.1.0"`. The plan lists it as a rename site while its own open-questions table decides to KEEP the `omp-rpc` distribution name. Doing both makes robomp's dependency unresolvable — `uv pip install` fails at resolve time, which is at least loud, and takes the entire bot down rather than degrading it.

Third, the inverse error: a broad `.omp` sweep across `python/**`. The `.omp*` family is 108 occurrences in 12 files, and among them `worker.py:145,168,209` and `entrypoint.sh:60,61,65,66,77-81` manage the CLI's OWN config dir under `/srv/agent-home`. Moving those off `.omp` points robomp's staging at a root the CLI is not reading, or stops it pre-creating the run directory the daemon needs. Contained to containers, and invisible to both the Python tests and `check:ts`.

Fourth, trusting a plan line number. All eight `test_sandbox.py` references in §3.3 are off by exactly one; editing at the planned lines edits the line above each target and leaves the assertion asserting the old name.

Fifth, and the quietest: mechanically renaming `test_client.py:1044,1061`. The test stays green under either name, so the item ships with no automated proof that the default moved — while a reviewer reading a green suite concludes the default was verified.
open_questions: Is the `omp-rpc` DISTRIBUTION name being renamed at all? This blocks the item and the plan leaves it open. The stated default is KEEP `omp-rpc` permanently, on the grounds that renaming breaks every existing `pip install omp-rpc`. If that default stands, then `python/omp-rpc/pyproject.toml:6` stays AND `python/robomp/pyproject.toml:22` must stay as a coupled consequence, AND `Dockerfile:164`'s `pip install /tmp/wheels/omp_rpc-*.whl` keeps resolving. If the answer is instead to rename, this item grows a release-ordering requirement (publish the new name before retiring the old) and needs a changelog note in that package — which AGENTS.md forbids writing unless explicitly asked. The conservative default is assumed throughout this spec, and it is the only assumption that leaves the tree installable.

Is the `robomp` DISTRIBUTION name being renamed? The plan's open-questions table asks only about `omp-rpc` and says nothing about `robomp`, yet `python/robomp/pyproject.toml:6` is the same class of decision — a published PyPI name where renaming breaks every existing install. This spec assumes KEEP, but the question is genuinely unasked rather than answered, and `robomp` also encodes the old brand ('robo' + 'omp') in a way `omp-rpc` does not.

What is the new domain, and does `python/omp-rpc/pyproject.toml:26` move with it? `Homepage = "https://omp.sh/"` is the same value as `APP_URL` at `packages/utils/src/dirs.ts:24`, which the risk table freezes until a new domain actually resolves. If N9 has not been decided by the time this item lands, `:26` must be left alone rather than renamed on a guess. The safe default here is to leave it and record why.

Are `python/omp-rpc/pyproject.toml:27,28` (`Repository` and `Documentation`, both `https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi`) in scope for any milestone? They carry the old org name but are invisible to `git grep -n 'omp'`, because the string `oh-my-pi` does not contain the substring `omp`. W7 targets `@oh-my-pi/` with a trailing slash and would not match them; W8a handles bare `"oh-my-pi"` in TypeScript. A URL in a Python manifest currently belongs to nobody. Default: leave them, and do not let a W7 pass reach them by accident.

Does robomp's staged agent home need migrating when W6 flips `CONFIG_DIR_NAME`? `worker.py:145,168,209` and `entrypoint.sh:60,61,65,66,77-81` manage `/srv/agent-home/.omp` — the CLI's own config dir. This spec keeps them on `.omp` because W4's dual-root reader still reads the legacy root, which makes the current arrangement correct during the transition. But if `config migrate` (W5) has run on a container's volume, the staged home becomes stale and robomp would populate a root nobody reads. Nobody currently owns that hand-off. Default: keep as-is and raise it at W6; the fix is not safe to make before W4's dual-root reader is proven.
